Typing and tooling. One behaviour fix, one type change, no API additions.

## Fixed

**A literal `null` JSON body is reported, not thrown.** All eight providers used
to fail on it identically with `Cannot read properties of null`, naming neither
the provider nor the cause. They now report "Provider returned no usable rates"
and the chain falls back as it should.

## Changed

**`Provider.handler` has a real signature.** It was typed `Function`, which
accepts anything callable and cannot be called safely. It is now
`(data: any) => rateObject`, which is what the readme has always documented, so
the only handlers affected are ones that were never conforming.

## Internal

Every place the library reads untrusted input, a vendor body or a
caller-supplied rate table, is typed `unknown` and narrowed explicitly rather
than typed `any` and dereferenced. That is the defect class behind the `null`
body above, and behind several bugs fixed in 2.1.0.

Type-aware linting now runs in CI and before publish, so the same class of
mistake fails a pull request rather than reaching a release.

## Repository

SECURITY.md said the supported major was 1.x. It is 2.x. The default workflow
token is now read-only, OpenSSF Scorecard runs weekly, and there are issue and
pull request templates.
